transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me today. 

Um... well, I guess I'm here because... my wife and my supervisor at the plant, they kind of pushed me to come in. It's really not a huge deal, I don't think, but they keep saying that I'm not listening to them. Like, they'll be talking straight to me, and I swear I'm trying to pay attention, but... a minute later I'll realize I only caught half of what they said. Then I end up having to ask them to say it all again. 

I feel terrible about it, because I really don't want to be disrespectful or make them mad. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not wasting your time with this.
Have you always struggled with this kind of inattentiveness, or is this something that has only started happening more recently?

Um, well... I guess I've always been a little, you know, on the go or maybe a bit scatterbrained? But nothing too bad, I don't think! It really only got this noticeable... I'd say about two years and two months ago. 

That's, um... that's when my wife started working outside the home. Before that, she kind of managed all the moving pieces for us, but when she took her job, I had to start handling a lot more of the daily schedule on my own. I really wanted to be helpful and take that off her plate, but... I guess that's when things started slipping. I feel terrible that I haven't just been able to step up and manage it better for her. I should be able to just keep it all straight, you know? 

Am I... is that the kind of information you need, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.
Over the past two years, have you felt a persistent sense of sadness, hopelessness, or a loss of interest in the activities you usually enjoy?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I mean, I get a little down on myself sometimes when I mess up the schedule or forget what my wife asked me to do, but... that's just normal, right? I definitely don't feel hopeless. 

I still really like doing things! I love playing softball with the guys from the plant on weekends, and... well, I guess I haven't been going as much lately, just because I keep double-booking myself or forgetting what time we're supposed to meet, but... I still *want* to go! I'm definitely not depressed or anything. I try to stay really positive. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I know I'm messing up, but I really am trying to keep a good attitude about it. Does that sound okay to you?
Outside of the trouble with your schedule, do you find that you spend a lot of your day feeling restless, keyed up, or worried about a wide range of different things in your life?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I'm a big worrier. I mean, I don't sit around stressing about everything, you know? I'm not really an anxious person. 

I do get a little... well, I guess maybe restless is an okay word for it? Like, sometimes I just feel like I need to be doing something, moving around, keeping busy. But I think that's just because I like to be productive! I don't want to just sit there doing nothing when there's stuff to be done. It's not like I'm pacing the floors worrying about bad things happening or anything like that. 

I just... I like to stay active. That's pretty normal for a guy my age, right? I hope that answers what you were asking. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Looking back at your time in elementary school, did you ever get in trouble or hear from your teachers that you were having trouble paying attention or sitting still in class?

Um, well... I mean, I guess I was a pretty energetic kid? Nothing too crazy, I don't think! Just, you know, normal boy stuff. 

But, um... yeah, I suppose my teachers did have to move my desk around a lot. I just had a lot of energy, and sitting still for that long was... well, it was hard for me. I'd get a little antsy. And sometimes I'd get a little too excited and just sort of blurt out the answers before they called on me. I didn't mean any disrespect by it! I was just eager, you know? 

And I guess I did get talked to a few times about, um... kind of wandering over and looking at what the other kids were doing, maybe interrupting them a bit. But that was all before middle school! I was just a little kid trying to be friendly and helpful. 

I really wasn't trying to be a troublemaker, I promise. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a bad kid, because I really wasn't!

In your daily life now—not just when you were a child—do you find that you frequently interrupt others while they are speaking or find it difficult to wait your turn in conversations or group settings?

Um, well... I try really hard to be polite when people are talking! But, um... I guess at the plant, I do have a little trouble with, well, stepping on toes sometimes. I just really want to be a good team player, you know? 

Like, if I see one of the guys working on something and I know a better way, I'll kind of... just step in. I might reach right in and fix their setup for them, or just start telling them how to do it. I don't really wait for them to ask for help, or wait my turn if we're supposed to be going down the line in a certain order. 

And, well... it actually causes some arguments sometimes. They get pretty frustrated with me for cutting into their jobs without being asked. I always feel really bad about it afterwards, because I'm honestly just trying to keep production moving and help them out! I really don't mean to be a know-it-all or anything. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad coworker. I just get so eager to help that I jump the gun before I think about it. Is that... do you think that makes sense? I just want to make sure you know I'm coming from a good place with it.
Do you find that you have these impulses to jump in or interrupt others, or feel that restless need to move, nearly every single day, both at work and at home?

Um... yeah, I guess it is pretty much every day. Both places, really. I, um... I hate to admit this, because I really pride myself on being a hard worker and a good provider, you know? But at work, it's actually gotten a little serious. I've, well... I've had some formal warnings about it from my supervisor. They worry that my jumping in like that could cause a safety problem on the line. I would never, ever want to put anyone in danger! I just get so focused on keeping things moving. But it happens enough that I really worry I could lose my job over it. Which is just so embarrassing to say out loud. I'm really trying to be more careful, I promise. 

And then at home... well, it's kind of the same story. I want to be a good dad and husband, but my wife and kids, they get pretty frustrated with me. I try to jump in and get things done, but my wife says I just end up disrupting all our routines instead of actually helping them run smoothly. I feel awful about it, because I'm honestly just trying to pitch in and be helpful, you know? 

I just... I hope you don't think I'm a careless guy or a bad father. I really do care about doing a good job and taking care of my family. Does that... I mean, does that make sense to you? I just want to be sure I'm explaining it right.

If you had to choose which one gives you more trouble in your daily life, would you say it is the difficulty with paying attention to details and instructions, or the tendency to act impulsively and feel restless?

Um, well... that's a tough one. I guess... I mean, the restless stuff is definitely there, like I said. But if I'm being completely honest—and I really want to give you the right answer here—it might actually be the attention part that's causing the most trouble right now. 

I just... well, I get so eager to keep the line moving, you know? I want to be fast and efficient for the team. But sometimes, because I'm trying to be so quick, I guess I sort of... rush through the quality checks a little bit. It's nothing huge! Just, um, missing little things. Like maybe a label is slightly off, or a fitting isn't tightened all the way. 

It's just that it happens... well, it happens a bit too often, I guess. My supervisor has had to pull me aside about it a few times because those little mistakes keep slipping past me. I always feel terrible when it happens, because I really do care about doing good work. I'm not trying to be sloppy, I promise! I just get moving so fast and my brain is already on the next step. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad worker. I'm really trying to slow down and double-check things more. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

You mentioned that the impulsivity and restlessness cause problems at work and home, but would you say that the impulsive behaviors and restlessness are just as disruptive to your daily life as the difficulties you have with attention and focus?

Um, well... I mean, I guess they both cause some hiccups, you know? But, um... if I really think about it, I don't know if I'd say the restless stuff is *just* as bad as the attention stuff. 

I mean, yeah, my wife gets a little annoyed when I'm pacing around or trying to fix things while she's cooking, and I know the guys at work get frustrated when I jump in. But... I don't know, maybe the attention stuff is a little more disruptive? Because that's what's actually messing up the product, you know? The other stuff is just me trying to be helpful and maybe having a little too much energy. 

I really don't want to make it sound like I'm completely out of control or anything. I'm honestly just trying to do my best in both areas. I hope I'm not confusing things by saying that. Does that make sense to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are going.
